label: Access itself
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the importable item itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name, it hands the item on as itself. The game uses the same name on other types (for example `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` in the activity windows), but never on this one.

label: Name
summary: The name of an item that can be imported in the map editor's import tool, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it next to the item's selection box in the import tool's list.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether an item of the map editor's import tool is selected for import.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the item's box, and its click sets the opposite with SetSelected.

label: Itself
summary: The importable item itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass an object on, for example `recipient.Self` or `Character.Self` as an argument; none of those lines is about this type.

label: Set selected
summary: Selects an item of the map editor's import tool for import, or unselects it.
details: It returns nothing and takes one yes or no value. Vanilla passes the opposite of IsSelected on click, so each click switches the item.

fields.name: argument 1
fields.text: Whether the item is to be selected.

label: Access itself
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the importable group itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. No line uses it on this type.

label: All in group selected
summary: Whether every item in a group of the import tool is selected for import.
details: Vanilla uses it as the checked state of the group's 'Import All' box in the map editor's import tool.

label: Item count
summary: The number of importable items in a group of the import tool, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows a group in the map editor's import tool only when this is more than 0.

label: Importable items
summary: The list of importable items in a group of the import tool.
details: Vanilla uses it as the list (`datamodel`) of the group's rows in the map editor's import tool; each row is one importable item. The game does not register its return type.

label: Group title
summary: The title of a group in the import tool, as text.
details: Vanilla shows it as the heading of the group in the map editor's import tool.

label: Has diff tool
summary: Whether a diff tool (a program that compares two versions of a file) can be opened for this group of the import tool.
details: Vanilla shows the group's 'Show Diff' button only when this is yes.

label: Is collapsed
summary: Whether a group of the import tool is folded up, its items hidden.
details: Vanilla hides the group's item list while this is yes, and its fold button shows the opposite state.

label: Group selection mixed
summary: Whether only some items of an import tool group are selected, so its 'select all' box is neither fully on nor off.
details: Vanilla shows an extra mark on the group's 'Import All' box when this is yes. That this mark means a partly selected group is read from the name.

label: Launch diff tool
summary: Opens the diff tool (a program that compares two versions of a file) for a group of the import tool.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the group's 'Show Diff' button, whose tooltip says it spawns the diff tool for this importable.

label: Itself
summary: The importable group itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass an object on, for example `recipient.Self` as an argument; none of those lines is about this type.

label: Toggle group selection
summary: Selects all items of an import tool group, or clears them all.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the group's 'Import All' box in the map editor's import tool.

label: Fold or unfold
summary: Folds a group of the import tool up, or opens it again.
details: It returns nothing. Vanilla runs it from the group's header and fold button in the map editor's import tool.

label: Access itself
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the important action item itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. No line uses it on this type.

label: Dismiss
summary: A GUI action that dismisses the important action entry (a notification in the HUD).
details: Vanilla runs it on both click and right click of a notification in `hud_notification_templates.gui`. That the entry then disappears is read from its name.

label: Action type
summary: The kind of important action the entry stands for; its return type is not registered.
details: Vanilla asks it whether the kind is dangerous (`GetActionType.IsDangerous`) in the conditions that decide which notification widget is shown.

label: Combined label
summary: The text label of an important action entry that stands for several actions combined.
details: Vanilla uses it in the text 'read/unread combined', where it is shown in italics. The meaning of 'combined' is read from its name.

label: Description
summary: The description of the important action entry, as text.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. The lines in the game that use `GetDescription` belong to other types (buildings, government types, activity types).

label: Label
summary: The short text label of the important action entry.
details: Vanilla shows it in the list of important actions, in a normal style once the entry is read and a medium style while it is unread.

label: Selection marker
summary: A text that marks the entry as selected.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. The game never uses it.

label: Tooltip
summary: The tooltip text of the important action entry.
details: Vanilla sets a notification's `tooltip` to it in `hud_notification_templates.gui`.

label: Is read
summary: Whether the important action entry has been read (yes or no).
details: Vanilla shows a widget only while it is not read (`Not(IsRead)`) and picks a text style by it. That `MarkAsRead` is what sets it is read from the names.

label: Is selected
summary: Whether the important action entry is currently selected (yes or no).
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `IsSelected` on other items (save game, bookmark, unit), not on this type.

label: Is unimportant
summary: Whether the important action entry is marked as not important (yes or no).
details: Vanilla combines it with the action type to decide which notification widget is shown: one for entries that are not unimportant and of a dangerous type, another for the safe type. What 'unimportant' means beyond its name is not stated.

label: Is visible
summary: Whether the important action entry should be shown (yes or no).
details: Vanilla uses it to set the visibility of notification widgets in `hud_notification_templates.gui`.

label: Mark as read
summary: A GUI action that marks the important action entry as read.
details: Vanilla runs it when the mouse enters the entry (`onmousehierarchyenter`), so just pointing at an entry counts as reading it.

label: On click
summary: A GUI action that runs the click handling of the important action entry.
details: Vanilla calls it from the `onclick` of notifications in `hud_notification_templates.gui`. What the click does for each action is decided by the game's code, which the input does not show.

label: Itself
summary: The important action entry itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass an object on, for example `Character.Self` as an argument; none of those lines is about this type.

label: Access itself
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the important action type itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. No line uses it on this type.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of the important action type; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `GetIcon` on other types (a DLC, an inspiration type) as a texture, not on this one.

label: Name
summary: The name of the important action type, as text; it takes one argument.
details: Going by its name and its text return type. The game's documentation does not say what the argument is. The lines in the game that use `GetName` belong to other types.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The one argument the function takes; the game does not describe it.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the important action type has an icon; its return type is not registered.

label: Is dangerous
summary: Whether this kind of important action counts as dangerous (yes or no).
details: Vanilla reaches it as `ImportantActionItem.GetActionType.IsDangerous` in the conditions that decide which notification widget is shown. What makes a kind dangerous is not stated.

label: Itself
summary: The important action type itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass an object on; none of those lines is about this type.

label: Owner
summary: The character who owns the inspiration; its return type is not registered.
details: Vanilla sets it as a data context in `hud.gui` and uses it in the inspiration tooltip. That the owner is a character is read from its use there.

label: Progress
summary: How far the inspiration has progressed, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla shows it as 'progress/10' in the progress tooltip and passes it, with the defines `MAX_PROGRESS` and `PROGRESS_FRAMES`, to a segmented chance bar in the HUD.

label: Progress chance
summary: The chance that the inspiration progresses, as a whole number.
details: Vanilla names it in the progress tooltip and in the estimated-time tooltip, and uses it for the segmented chance bar in the HUD. Whether the number is a percent is read from its use.

label: Sponsor
summary: The character who sponsors the inspiration; its return type is not registered.
details: Vanilla shows the sponsor's name in the tooltip and checks whether the sponsor is valid and whether it is the local player.

label: Type
summary: The type of the inspiration; its return type is not registered.
details: Vanilla asks it for its icon (`GetType.GetIcon`) to draw the inspiration in the HUD.

label: Is complete
summary: Whether the inspiration is completed (yes or no).
details: Vanilla shows a part of `hud.gui` and of the inspirations window only when the sponsor is valid and the inspiration is not complete.

label: Make scope
summary: Turns the inspiration into a script scope, so that text commands can work with it.
details: Going by its name and its `Scope` return type. The name `MakeScope` is used 1043 times in the game's files on many types; no shown line names this type.

label: Itself
summary: The inspiration itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Vanilla passes it on as an argument: `InGameBottomBar.ToggleSelectedInspiration( Inspiration.Self )`.

label: Access itself
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the inspiration type itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. No line uses it on this type.

label: Icon
summary: The icon of the inspiration type; its return type is not registered.
details: Vanilla uses it as a texture, as `Inspiration.GetType.GetIcon` in `hud.gui`.

label: Has icon
summary: Whether the inspiration type has an icon; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `HasIcon` on other types (a concept tooltip, a law), not on this one.

label: Itself
summary: The inspiration type itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. Vanilla uses `Self` on other types to pass an object on; none of those lines is about this type.

label: Access itself
summary: A GUI function that gives access to the inspirations window itself; its return type is not registered.
details: Going by its name. No line uses it on this type.

label: Clear new inspirations
summary: A GUI action that clears the 'new' marks of the inspirations in the inspirations window.
details: Going by its name. The game never uses it.

label: Clear selected inspiration
summary: A GUI action that clears the inspiration selected in the inspirations window.
details: Vanilla runs it on click in `gui/window_inspirations.gui`.
